title: SharePoint: mark sites as authoritative so Copilot prioritises their content
summary: The briefing passes: its controls, limits and roadmap details are supported, and its unresolved defaults and integration questions remain undocumented. Two minor corrections remain: report the cmdlet reference's different licensing wording, and remove the checklist's sharing-control instruction that has no corresponding table row.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The authoritative sites page says a Microsoft Copilot licence is required and links to the SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites.
claims.quote: Licensing: A Microsoft Copilot license is required. (See Prerequisites for SharePoint Advanced Management.)

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The feature is included through the documented Copilot-backed SharePoint Advanced Management entitlement rather than a separately named authoritative-sites licence.
claims.quote: If your organization has at least one Microsoft Copilot license assigned to a user, your SharePoint administrators automatically receive access to SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities to support your Copilot deployment.
claims.fix: Keep the entitlement account, but add: 'The Set-SPOSite -IsAuthoritative reference instead describes "an admin with a Copilot license", whereas the Advanced Management prerequisites say the licensed user does not need to be a SharePoint administrator.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/set-sposite?view=sharepoint-ps beside this qualification; it is already in sources.
